mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS declines by more than 0.25% in the past month, the 5-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 4.5% signals weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in less than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is not rising sufficiently, the market anticipates delayed monetary tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS does not rise (or rises less than 0.25%), the 20-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong industrial production growth (INDPRO above 105), the market anticipates robust corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO exceeds 105, the 20-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand for durable goods, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST rises by more than 0.5% in the past month, the 60-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly inflation rate above 3.5% (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation that may lead to aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in less than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) is slowing and unemployment (UNRATE) is rising, the market anticipates a weakening labor market and reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth slows (declines by more than 0.3% in the past month) and UNRATE rises (by more than 0.1pp), the 20-day forward returns are negative in less than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high unemployment (UNRATE above 4.5%), the market anticipates reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, the 5-day forward returns are negative in less than 60% of cases.
